A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MrSteve research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A-P. Text comparison and visual inspection support a reliable comparison throughout.

before.justification: v3 reports original Minecraft experiments on exploration, sequential task solving, memory and navigation in Section 4, plus ablations and hierarchical planning experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results, including Table 1, Figures 5-7 and the appendix experiments.

M1.justification: PEM, mode selection, hierarchical exploration, VPT-Nav and Algorithms 1-8 retain the same procedures. The task-conditioned exploration and center-embedding memory variants already appear in v3 Appendices N and P. Terminology corrections do not change these methods.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Minecraft exploration, ABA-Sparse, ABA-Random, SEQ(4), memory-navigation, long-horizon and hierarchical planning scenarios. No dataset, task or environmental coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged within corresponding experiments, including Steve-1, Plan4MC-based methods, FIFO/place/event memory variants and the heuristic navigator in Table 7. The DEPS comparisons are also retained.

E3.justification: Map sizes, task horizons, memory budgets, evaluation metrics and training settings remain unchanged in Section 4 and the appendices. Appendix C.1 grammatically revises the inventory-based success criterion without changing its meaning.

E4.justification: Both retain the top-k and cluster-size studies, navigation architecture and KL-loss ablations, task-conditioned exploration analysis, memory-capacity sweeps and center-only memory investigation in Appendices J and L-P. Their experimental questions and evidence are unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix C.2.1 retains 100 episodes with different seeds for ordinary tasks and five runs with standard-error reporting for long-horizon tasks. Table 4 retains averages and standard errors over 1,000 queries. No statistical reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Corresponding tables and plots retain their numerical entries, curves, rankings and findings throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 9 retains DEPS bed-task success rates of 27% with Steve-1 and 50% with MrSteve.

T1.justification: Mathematical definitions, Equations (1)-(3) and computational-complexity arguments are retained. Replacing x or o with i for already-described pixel observations in Sections 3 and 4.3 standardizes notation without changing mathematical reasoning or assumptions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about low-level episodic memory, PEM and improved exploration and task solving. Shortening the expansion of MrSteve and removing duplicated conclusion text do not alter the contributions.

C2.justification: Mechanistic interpretations and applicability limits are unchanged. Section 5 retains limitations concerning planner access to PEM, underground navigation, challenging terrain and exact positional information; Appendix P retains the performance-efficiency tradeoff of center-only storage.

D1.justification: Hardware and runtime information, pseudocode, memory and training hyperparameters, task prompts, project link and code-release statements remain unchanged. Correcting 'K++ Means' to 'K-Means++' in Appendix E.1 adds no implementation information.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning against prior controllers, planners and memory systems remain unchanged in Section 2, Appendix A and the references.

P1.justification: v5 corrects scattered grammar and spelling, standardizes notation and algorithm names, changes 'MemoryRecall Steve-1' to 'MemoryRecall Steve', and removes a duplicated opening in Section 6. Publication, affiliation and funding text are updated; section organization remains intact.

P2.justification: The same 18 figures and 11 tables are retained. Changes include publication headers, minor caption corrections in Tables 4 and 8, and small spacing or positioning adjustments, including Table 7. The visual evidence is unchanged.

improvement.justification: Removing the duplicated conclusion opening, standardizing pixel-observation notation and correcting appendix terminology and grammar modestly improve clarity. Scientific evidence, reproducibility information and limitations remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited to editorial quality.
